lesson_body:
Welcome to Day 2 of our Counting Base Unit! Today, we will dive deeper into the world of numbers and explore how we can combine them in exciting ways. In our last lesson, we recognized numbers from 0 to 20. We played games with counting objects and enjoyed exploring different ways to represent these numbers using pictures and tallies. Today, we will explore how to count in groups of ten, which helps us build a strong foundation for understanding larger numbers in the future.

Let’s start by understanding what counting in groups of ten means. When we count to 10, we can think of these as a special group of numbers. For example, if you have a set of 30 small toys, you can count them more easily if you group them in sets of ten. So instead of counting 1, 2, 3… all the way to 30, you can say 10, 20, 30! This saves time and makes counting more fun!

To help us visualize these groups, we will use ten frames. A ten frame is a simple tool that shows how many items fit into a group of ten. You will each receive a ten frame chart that has spaces for ten squares. Let’s fill in our first ten frame together! If I have 7 apples, how many more do I need to make a full ten frame? Correct! We would need 3 more apples! This way, we can see that 7 plus 3 equals 10. Through this, we can learn to recognize numbers that easily combine to 10.

As we continue, let’s think about the number 20. How many ten frames will we need to show the number 20? Yes, we will need two ten frames! Let’s draw these together. Remember, each full ten frame represents ten. So, when we fill two ten frames, we show 20 items in total! This visual representation helps you see how numbers can be composed and decomposed, making your math journey more manageable and exciting.

To make things even fun, we will play a counting game where you will partner up and practice counting items in groups of ten. This is a great way to develop teamwork and communication skills while enhancing your math skills. At the end of the lesson, we will share what we learned, and you will have a chance to show your friends how you can count in the base ten system with your ten frames. Remember, counting is not just about numbers; it is about understanding how those numbers connect and work together!
interactive_assignment: For our hands-on activity today, you will create your very own Counting Book! Gather ten small objects from around your home or classroom, like buttons, stones, or pieces of paper. Arrange them into groups of ten and decorate each page of your book. On the first page, draw or glue a picture of your first group of ten objects. On the second page, create a new group of ten objects. In this book, as you explore the different groups, make sure to write down how many objects are on each page (e.g., 10, 20, etc.). When you finish your Counting Book, share it with a friend or family member and explain how you counted the objects in groups of ten. This will help you practice your counting and show others how much fun counting can be!

daily_assessment.question: If you have 8 crayons and want to fill a ten frame, how many more crayons do you need?
